quiz2.prompt: A hypothetical nondispersive wave model has speed v=1/√(με). Its ε is four times a reference value while μ is unchanged. What happens to the model speed?
quiz2.explanation: The product με increases by four, so its square root doubles and the reciprocal speed halves. This is a hypothetical parameter comparison; the SI vacuum speed of light is exactly 299792458 m/s.

quiz10.prompt: An antenna carries a perfectly steady direct current after all turn-on transients have ended. What radiative far-field term does that time-independent source produce?
quiz10.explanation: Time-independent charge and current distributions have static electric and magnetic fields, not a time-dependent radiative far field. Switching the source on or off is a different problem and can produce transient radiation.
